invariants: At most one active cycle at a time in both the on-chain coordinator (Lifecycle != EMPTY/PAYOUT_COMMITTED blocks new authorizeFunding) and the operator state file (activeCycleId null <=> no active runner).

Every accepted cycleId gets a distinct CREATE2 escrow; escrow address is deterministic from (coordinator, usdg, hook, routeExecutor, cycleId) and independently recomputable via computeCycleEscrow before authorization.

A FAILED cycle's escrow is permanently quarantined: only authorizeFundingAfterFailure with the exact failedCycleId + failureReceiptDigest can authorize a successor, and the successor gets a fresh cycleId/nonce/escrow; the failed escrow itself is never revisited.

Nonces, cycleIds, payoutIds and returnReceiptDigests are each single-use for their whole domain lifetime (consumedNonces/consumedCycles/consumedPayoutIds/consumedReturnReceiptDigests mappings never cleared).

Exact-delta balance checks surround every escrow transfer (before/after balanceOf comparisons in both PegCycleReturnEscrow._transferExact and PegCycleVault.executeOutbound/consumePayoutAuthorization) so unsolicited/surplus USDG in an escrow can never be swept into principal or payout.

Deadline renewal (renewFundingAuthorizationDeadline / renewPayoutAuthorizationDeadline) may change only expiresAt and nonce; every other field must be byte-identical to the currently active authorization (_fundingSubjectDigest/_payoutSubjectDigest zero out expiresAt/nonce before hashing for comparison).

Operator state file: revision-CAS (stale expectedRevision rejected), exclusive 0600 lock with PID+UUID ownership, atomic tmp+rename+fsync(dir); a draft and a frozen plan can never coexist; a pending draft/plan must reuse neither a terminal cycleId/nonce/returnAccount nor (for frozen plans) a terminal onchainCycleId.

assertFreshIdentity (control.mjs:146) is enforced both at prepare-time and start-time against the full terminalCycles history, so a stale draft cannot slip through if a terminal record was added between prepare and start.

Terminal observation (recordTerminalObservation) requires the runner to have no unresolved external intent, requires FAILED lifecycle only after locally-evidenced outbound-finalized-or-later progress, and requires PAYOUT_COMMITTED only from a 'closed' stage with payoutFundingPrepared true -- prevents a caller from asserting a terminal state the local journal never actually reached.
stateTransitions: On-chain PegCycleVault.Lifecycle: EMPTY -> FUNDED (confirmFunding) -> OUTBOUND (executeOutbound) -> RETURNED (authorizePayout) -> PAYOUT_COMMITTED (consumePayoutAuthorization) -> [new cycle, back to EMPTY-equivalent via fresh cycleId] ; or OUTBOUND -> FAILED (recordTerminalFailure) -> [successor cycle via authorizeFundingAfterFailure]. FUNDED and RETURNED each support an in-place deadline-only self-loop via renewal.

Operator local plan: DRAFT --freeze--> FROZEN --start--> ACTIVE --crash/restart--> ACTIVE (same cycleId/planDigest) --unresolved attempt--> RECONCILE_REQUIRED --verified reconciliation--> ACTIVE --payout committed--> PAYOUT_COMMITTED (terminal) ; ACTIVE --verified terminal failure--> FAILED (terminal) ; FROZEN(expired, never started) --abandon-expired--> EXPIRED_UNSTARTED (terminal, no journal). PAYOUT_COMMITTED/FAILED/EXPIRED_UNSTARTED --fresh id+nonce--> DRAFT. No FAILED->ACTIVE and no RECONCILE_REQUIRED->retry transitions exist anywhere in the code.

autonomyGaps: No scheduler / interval loop of any kind. ADR-0020 and the design doc explicitly reject 'Build a dashboard and automatic pack strategy first' and the owner-approval JSONs explicitly re-defer P1-011 (dashboard/scheduler/unattended automation). There is no code path that fires every N minutes; every transition (prepare/freeze/start/resume/reconcile) is an operator-invoked CLI call.

No dashboard or any UI -- CLI-only, single operator, single terminal session implied by the file lock (one process at a time; concurrent invocations serialize/contend, they do not queue for a 'change interval' or 'restart stuck cycle' UI action).

No automatic pack purchase selection -- 'packs list' + manual 'cycle prepare --input <file with chosen pack>' only; quantity is hardcoded to 1 and turbo hardcoded to false at the schema-validation level (cycle-plan.mjs assertDraftBody throws if quantity!=1 or turbo!=false).

No real sale/buyback execution path -- the design doc's 'Funding and return flow' step 4 ('Outbound execution asks the escrow to send... to the immutable route executor') and step 5 ('Exact attributable returned USDG arrives in that escrow') describe the contract-level custody only; the actual Collector Crypt pack-buy/open/buyback and Robinhood<->Solana bridge integration remains INTEGRATION_PENDING per product/SOURCE_BOUNDARY.md, unchanged by this branch (only the return *destination* changed from vault to per-cycle escrow).

No real on-chain terminal-state reader -- OperatorControl's terminalObservationVerifier is an unimplemented stub that throws by default (control.mjs:182-184); a real deployment needs an injected verifier the branch does not provide, so 'restart/kick cycles that got stuck' (owner's dashboard requirement) has no automated on-chain confirmation path today, only a manually-supplied and manually-signed fixture observation.

No pro-rata distribution automation -- vault-payout-authorization.mjs and reconcile.mjs prepare the payout authorization/Merkle root off-chain, but nothing in this branch triggers or schedules that preparation; it is still an operator-run compiler step (consistent with Phase 1's design, untouched here).
No community-facing status surface -- 'cycle status' is a CLI JSON dump (operator-status.v1 schema), not a hosted/public-facing view; no web server or API exists in the diff.

Even the manual, single-cycle flow the branch DOES implement is explicitly 'no external action authorized' at every layer (ADR-0020 header, PRD, SOURCE_BOUNDARY, owner-approval JSONs, qa review 'externalActionsPerformed: false') -- so even running this branch as-is against a real Robinhood Chain deployment funds nothing and buys no packs; it only exercises the local state machine and fixture-signed observations.

Net effect vs. the owner's target: this branch delivers roughly the custody-isolation and manual-repeat-cycle building blocks a future scheduler could sit on top of (per-cycle escrow prevents a stuck/failed cycle from poisoning the next one), but it delivers zero of the 'every 20 minutes, automatically, dashboard-adjustable, with buy/open/sell/distribute actually executing' requirement; per ADR-0020/PRD it explicitly requires 'a fresh spec revision plus owner approval' before that work can start, matching the repo-established Phase 2 deferral fact.
